summary: New personal agents head to head (Instinct, GrokBot, Muse), a trending repos round-up (code review, skill packs, worktrees, context saving) and new releases (Claude Slides, Notion skills, Vercel tools). Best for Charlie: Agent Skills, I Have ADHD, hyperframes.

tools.name: Instinct
tools.what: Free personal AI agent you text through iMessage or WhatsApp; it researches and can buy for you.
tools.shown: Texted it an Airbnb search; it answered 5 to 10 minutes later with links and a text list, no browser view.
tools.quote: Instinct is an agent that is a free agent um that is all the rage right now.
tools.check: Free 'for now' while VC funded; invite-only signup; one user said it kept his email data after he cancelled.

vs.gap: Not tested for our jobs (Claude Code, AI OS, YouTube); unknown whether it can run repeatable tasks or touch files.

tools.name: GrokBot
tools.what: Paid personal agent with a visible browser, reusable skills, shareable personas and multi-step processes.
tools.shown: Ran the same Airbnb search; sent browser screenshots and a map and let the user take over the browser.
tools.quote: Grockbot is paid and they've reduced their entry price to about 20 bucks, but you'll burn through the 20 bucks pretty quickly.
tools.check: Price: about 20 dollars entry but said to burn through quickly.

vs.gap: Unknown how its shareable skills compare with Claude Code skills, or whether it is worth paying for when we already have Claude Code.

tools.name: Meta Muse
tools.what: Meta's free-tier personal agent: clean tables, fast replies, opens the Airbnb app, can now make phone calls.
tools.shown: Same Airbnb search: table of ratings and cancellation dates, near-instant follow-ups, then a live Mexico City browse.
tools.quote: Also, it was faster than everybody else.
tools.check: Free tier then charges more the more you use it.

vs.gap: Not tested for building or running an AI OS; unknown how custom connectors work or what it costs after the free tier.

tools.name: Hyperagent
tools.what: Agent platform Andrew uses at his company because it handles teams of people.
tools.quote: Hyper Agent I find to be really good at that.
tools.check: Only a one-line mention; the detail is in a separate video.

vs.gap: Not shown here; we don't know its price or whether it suits a one-person channel.

tools.name: Open Code Review
tools.what: Alibaba's tool that checks code for security problems and can write an HTML report; has a CLI and skills.
tools.shown: A linked demo found a deliberately planted plain-text password and made an HTML report with one command.
tools.quote: This is the thing that will let you check your code to find common or maybe even uncommon problems.
tools.check: Demo was a clip, not run live by the hosts.

vs.gap: Not run by us; unknown how to wire it to a git hook for this repo or whether it adds value for non-code files.

tools.name: I Have ADHD
tools.what: A single skill file that makes the AI answer short and easy to scan; 47,000 stars.
tools.shown: A clip of the Claude web app before and after the slash command: answer became much shorter.
tools.quote: It's scannable so you understand it.
tools.check: Star count (47,000) is the host's claim.

vs.gap: Not tried in Charlie's own sessions; unknown if it clashes with the plain UK English and Now/Done when rules in AGENTS.md.

tools.name: God's Eye View
tools.what: Interactive map joining open public data (traffic, CCTV cameras, flights); also available as a Pinocchio app.
tools.shown: A clip of the map with TomTom traffic, camera previews on hover and live flights.
tools.quote: it pulls together all the open data that's available online

vs.gap: Fun demo only; no link to Charlie's jobs and not tried.

tools.name: ECC
tools.what: Huge pack of engineering workflows and skills (plan, test-driven development) for coding agents; 261,000 stars.
tools.shown: A clip of the creator running plan mode then the TDD workflow before building.
tools.quote: It's a way to get decades of of experience from other software engineers and inject that into your uh coding sessions.
tools.check: Star count (261,000) is the host's claim.

vs.gap: Unknown how heavy it is to install and whether a beginner needs a pack this big next to Agent Skills.

tools.name: Context Mode
tools.what: Runs side work in a sandbox and hands only the answer back so the main session stays short and saves tokens.
tools.shown: Explained on the README; the clips of someone measuring token savings were skipped as too long.
tools.quote: makes the focus of your main conversation stay on the work instead of all the side work
tools.check: Token-saving figures not shown on screen.

vs.gap: Savings are unproven; we don't know the real token saving or whether it works with Claude Code hooks here.

tools.name: WeKnora
tools.what: Tencent tool that turns your files into a searchable AI knowledge graph and wiki.
tools.shown: A clip of the graph and linked wiki pages (in Chinese).
tools.quote: it seems like Obsidian plus rag plus AI plus a graph database.

vs.gap: Unknown setup effort and whether it beats the plain markdown brain files we already use.

tools.name: OpenAI Plugins
tools.what: OpenAI's open plugin packs (e.g. Figma); Claude can convert them or use a connector.
tools.shown: Browsed the repo and discussed whether Claude Code can use them.
tools.quote: when you start to install these plugins, it's like installing software on your computer and you're giving it access to all your data, your code, your secret keys.
tools.check: Security warning: plugins can run code. Star count (6 to 7 thousand) is a claim.

vs.gap: Unknown whether a Codex plugin works unchanged in Claude Code; we install plugins only with Charlie's OK.

tools.name: Worktrunk
tools.what: Command line tool that makes git worktrees (separate folders) easy so several AI agents don't edit the same files.
tools.shown: Explained on the README plus a linked walkthrough video.
tools.quote: Five agents, five copies of your project, one tool.

vs.gap: Not tried; unknown if it helps one-at-a-time work like Charlie's, and git worktrees are an advanced topic.

tools.name: Agent Skills
tools.what: Addy Osmani's set of skills run in order: spec, plan, build, test, review, ship; 95,000 stars.
tools.shown: Walked through the order of the workflow on the README.
tools.quote: you're meant to run these skills in this order
tools.check: Star count (95,000) is the host's claim.

vs.gap: Unknown which of the 25 skills are worth installing first for a beginner and how they fit our own skills.

tools.quote: This one is centered around projects and in one project you might use yeah five different types of agents.
tools.check: Audience submission, brand new.

vs.gap: Not tried; unknown if it is stable or useful with just one agent.
